title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Recital Program. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean mobile event list with cards, a blue Add button, and a calendar icon on every row.
canonCard.viewport: Stacked event cards, search at top, primary button bottom-right — the Eventbrite/Meetup arrangement at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other community calendar by design.

options.label: Recital Program
options.lineage: Folded choir and school recital inserts with named performers and clock times
options.thesis: This week is a printed program: day as movement, event as billed piece, youth as the names under the title.
options.viewport: Phone: a program header (Celina Ward, This week), then SATURDAY as a movement title, compact billed rows, Add event in thumb reach.
options.risk: Can feel like church stationery if the green/crimson pairing goes timid and games look like hymns.

raised.raise: An opened event owns the viewport; the rest of the program recedes until you close it.
One type family at stepped sizes: day, title, youth names, clock — no extra chrome for hierarchy.
Each row carries a duration measure so a two-hour game does not look like a ten-minute number.
Scale contrast alone does the work; no eyebrows, no icon-and-label stacks.

options.label: Fridge Calendar
options.lineage: Kitchen command-center pads and magnet calendars
options.thesis: The family fridge: this week is already on the door, thumb-smeared, with the next game written in marker.
options.viewport: A weekly pad filling the phone: days as stacked blocks, events handwritten on the lines, Add event as a fat marker button.
options.risk: This is the familiar landing for a family calendar — effective, and the direction most runs in this category choose.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: Segmented boarding pass plus live departure board
options.thesis: Events rank by start time like departures; past ones drop off; an open event is a stub ticket you can file on your calendar.
options.viewport: A time-ordered board of compact rows; tap a row and it becomes a ticket with Add to calendar as the scan action.
options.case: Holds product clarity (time rank, past drop off, identity-preserving rows) but loses audience identification — an airport is not the ward.
options.risk: Can feel like travel software unless the ticket language stays youth/event, not flight/gate.

options.label: Season Folio
options.lineage: Botanical plates that keep one scale and one baseline across stages
options.thesis: Each day is a plate on a shared baseline; events sit at the same scale so Saturday’s game and Sunday’s choir can be compared at a glance.
options.viewport: Day plates banded on one line; titles and youth names as captions under each specimen row, not inside cards.
options.case: Holds product clarity (comparable rows, shared measure) but families do not identify with a botanical folio.
options.risk: Garden-plate romance can smother the schedule job if plates become illustration instead of days.

options.label: One-event feed
options.lineage: Full-bleed vertical media with a right-rail of actions
options.thesis: One event fills the phone; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: A single event owns the screen; Add to calendar and Add youth sit in a right rail.
options.case: Parents cannot scan this week; a feed hides the schedule.
options.risk: Reads as social video, not a ward calendar.

options.label: Bitmap specimen
options.lineage: Emigre coarse pixel letterforms at poster scale
options.thesis: The week set in proud low-resolution display type.
options.viewport: A towering pixel day-name over dense event columns.
options.case: Families do not identify with type-foundry specimens; bitmap type hurts clock times.
options.risk: Novelty type over the scan job.

options.label: Dance score
options.lineage: Labanotation staff read upward, duration as block length
options.thesis: The week as a vertical score where each event’s height is how long it lasts.
options.viewport: A center staff with events as duration blocks; time flowing upward.
options.case: Time-upward fights how a parent reads a calendar.

options.label: Live type specimen
options.thesis: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone, with the week’s names as the specimen.
options.viewport: A giant day letter; events as a glyph grid underneath.
options.case: A foundry page is not a schedule; the job disappears.
